advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen test_change_refs_are_forced_without_widening_replication_scope to assert that NO push spec other than refs/changes/* carries a leading '+', and that no refs/meta/* push spec exists.
evidence: The test name asserts 'without_widening_replication_scope' and the config comment (infra/gerrit/replication.config:64-66) states the force is 'deliberately scoped to refs/changes/* — NOT refs/heads/* or wildcard refs/*', but no assertion forbids a NEW leading-'+' on any non-changes refspec or a new refs/meta push.

tests/scripts/test_gerrit_replication_config.py:26-31 assert only that specific strings are present/absent: `assert "+refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*" in specs` ... `assert "refs/*:refs/*" not in specs` — there is no assertion that every spec beginning with '+' equals the change-refs spec

Contract under review (infra/gerrit/replication.config:16-18): 'The refs/changes/* refspec is the only exception: it is force-updated' and docs/adr/0021: 'The refs/changes/* namespace is the only forced refspec'

Named violating input: adding `push = +refs/heads/release/*:refs/heads/release/*` to the [remote "github"] block leaves all six spec assertions and all three body substring assertions green, yet clobbers a branch namespace's fast-forward-only safety
search over tests/ for `startswith("+")` and force-count assertions returns no guard elsewhere
advisory.finding: The new invariant test claims to preserve branch/tag/feature one-way-door safety but only checks presence of the forced change-ref spec and absence of two hard-coded strings; it would still PASS if a future edit added a forced branch/tag/meta refspec (e.g. '+refs/heads/main:refs/heads/main' or 'push = +refs/meta/*'), so the safety property is not actually enforced.
merged_from: The invariant test asserts the specific refspecs present/absent but never asserts that refs/changes/* is the ONLY force-prefixed ('+') refspec. A regression that ADDS a new forced namespace (e.g. `push = +refs/heads/release/*:refs/heads/release/*`) would pass every existing assertion while violating the one-way-door force-exclusivity contract the diff reaffirms ('The refs/changes/* namespace is the only forced refspec'; 'branch/tag/feature refs remain non-force').
advisory.suggested_fix: Add: assert [s for s in specs if s.startswith('+')] == ['+refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*'] and assert not any('refs/meta' in s for s in specs).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the ADR-0021 mirror-visibility wording: the amendment says 'org-private mirror' while the Consequences section still says 'public GitHub mirror' / 'already public in the public Gerrit project'.
evidence: docs/adr/0021-replication-change-refs.md:26: The operator accepted the org-private mirror visibility trade-off and the scoped force trade-off
docs/adr/0021-replication-change-refs.md:44: - Unmerged/abandoned patchsets become visible on the public GitHub mirror as
docs/adr/0021-replication-change-refs.md:45: `refs/changes/*` (they are already public in the public Gerrit project, so no new disclosure).
advisory.finding: The ADR-0021 amendment introduced by this diff describes an 'org-private mirror visibility trade-off', contradicting the unchanged Consequences bullet that states abandoned patchsets 'become visible on the public GitHub mirror ... they are already public in the public Gerrit project (no new disclosure)'. The doc now asserts both a private and a public mirror.
